sections.title: Form and range
sections.text: Dawn redwood is a large deciduous conifer native to a restricted area of central China and now planted elsewhere. It can reach about 35–43 m and has reddish-brown bark.

sections.title: Branchlets, leaves and cones
sections.text: The branchlets and leaves are arranged in opposite pairs. The soft leaves fall in autumn. Pollen cones and seed cones are separate; the rounded seed cones hang from short stalks.

sections.title: Uses
sections.text: The species is mainly grown as an ornamental tree. No relevant food use was found in the sources consulted.
